symptom: Forward Evaluation Vault 0.1's runtime instant regex and exactInstant schema accepted unbounded fractional-second digits, while the separate v0.2 claimed-instant helper already rejects more than 64 digits and timestamps longer than 90 characters. A deterministic synthetic Node 22.16.0 reproduction showed regex and Date.parse acceptance for 65 and 100000 fractional digits. This is an avoidable caller-controlled validation/allocation surface, not an observed external attack, private-data exposure, production defect or settlement authority.
lesson: A resource bound fixed in a v0.2 claimed-instant helper does not automatically cover the older Forward Vault v0.1 record and schema boundary. Both versions process untrusted claimed clocks; audit each independently rather than inferring safety from one green suite.
guardrail: For the research-only Forward Vault v0.1 instant validator, reject inputs longer than 90 characters and fractional seconds longer than 64 ASCII digits before Date.parse or chronology comparison. Mirror maxLength 90 and fractional {1,64} in the v0.1 schema, preserve valid submillisecond comparisons, and regression-test 64-digit acceptance, 65-digit rejection, and a bounded synthetic oversized input. This is structural resource control only; no source time, scoring or production authority.
